#!/usr/bin/env bash
while IFS=, read -r name email role; do
  username=$(echo "$name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -d ' ')
  password=$(openssl rand -base64 12)
  sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash "$username" && echo "$username:$password" | sudo chpasswd

out_dir=/data/incoming

  if [[ $file == *.zip ]]; then
    if unzip -o "$in_dir/$file" -d "$out_dir" >> /var/log/unzip.log 2>&1; then

  fi
done

tree_match() {
  local dir="$1" pat="$2"
  find "$dir" -type f -name "$pat" | while IFS= read -r file; do
    depth=$(echo "$file" | awk -F'/' '{print NF-1}')
    indent=$(printf '%*s' $((depth*2)) '')

    echo "${indent}$(basename "$file") ($size bytes)"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

declare -A seen
find /data -type f -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  hash=$(md5sum "$file" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [[ -v seen[$hash] ]]; then
    original=${seen[$hash]}
    rm "$file" && ln "$original" "$file" && echo "Replaced $file with hard link to $original"
  else
    seen[$hash]="$file"
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/auth.log
while sleep 30; do
  ips=$(grep 'Failed password' "$log" | awk '{print $(NF-3)}' | sort -u)
  for ip in $ips; do
    if ! grep -q "sshd: $ip" /etc/hosts.deny; then
      echo "sshd: $ip" >> /etc/hosts.deny
      echo "Blocked SSH brute‑force from $ip" | mail -s "SSH Blocked" admin@example.com
    fi
  done
done

backup_dir(){
  dir="$1"
  base=$(basename "$dir")
  ts=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
  tarball="/backup/${base}_${ts}.tar.gz"
  tar -czf "$tarball" -C "$(dirname "$dir")" "$base"

  echo "$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') BACKUP $dir -> $tarball ($size)" >> /var/log/backup.log
}

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
count_commits() {
  while read -r repo; do
    tmp=$(mktemp -d)
    git clone --depth 1 "$repo" "$tmp" > /dev/null 2>&1
    cd "$tmp"
    cnt=$(git rev-list --count --since='1 month ago' HEAD)
    echo -e "${repo}	${cnt}"
    cd - > /dev/null
    rm -rf "$tmp"
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
inotifywait -m -e close_write --format "%w%f" /incoming |\
  while read -r file; do
    [[ "$file" == *.tar.gz ]] || continue
    if tar -tzf "$file" &>/dev/null; then
      mv "$file" /var/archives/validated/
    else
      mv "$file" /var/archives/corrupt/
    fi
  done

command:
clone_latest_tag() {
  local url="$1"
  local repo_name=$(basename "$url" .git)
  mkdir -p /opt/repos && cd /opt/repos
  git clone "$url"
  cd "$repo_name"
  latest_tag=$(git describe --tags $(git rev-list --tags --max-count=1))
  git checkout "$latest_tag"
  commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
  echo "$(date +'%F %T') $repo_name $latest_tag $commit" >> /opt/repos/clones.log
}

Create a Bash function that monitors a given directory for new files (using inotifywait), and when a new file appears, computes its MD5 checksum, appends the filename and checksum to /var/log/file_checksums.log, and moves the file to an archive directory preserving the original subdirectory structure.
command:
watch_new(){
  watch_dir="$1"
  archive_dir="/var/archive"
  mkdir -p "$archive_dir"
  inotifywait -m -e create --format "%w%f" "$watch_dir" | while read -r newfile; do
    checksum=$(md5sum "$newfile" | awk '{print $1}')
    echo "$(date +%F_%T) $newfile $checksum" >> /var/log/file_checksums.log
    rel=${newfile#${watch_dir}/}
    dest="$archive_dir/$(dirname "$rel")"
    mkdir -p "$dest"
    mv "$newfile" "$dest/"
  done
}

    for file in "$in_dir"/*.csv; do
        [ -e "$file" ] || continue
        if curl -s -X POST -F "file=@$file" https://api.example.com/upload; then
            echo "$(date +'%F %T') SUCCESS $file" >> "$log_file"

    done

done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
counter=0
start=0
tail -F /var/log/syslog | while read -r line; do
  if echo "$line" | grep -q 'kernel panic'; then
    echo "$(date +%F\\%T) $line" >> panic.log
    now=$(date +%s)
    if ((counter==0)); then start=$now; fi
    ((counter++))
    if ((counter>=3 && now-start<=600)); then
      echo "Critical: 3 kernel panics detected, rebooting..." | wall
      /sbin/reboot
    fi
  fi
done

Create a Bash loop that pings a list of hosts from hosts.txt every 30 seconds, logs latency to /var/log/ping.log with timestamps, and triggers a webhook if any host is unreachable for 3 consecutive attempts.
command:
while :; do
  while IFS= read -r host; do
    if ping -c1 -W1 "$host" >/dev/null; then
      echo "$(date +%F_%T) $host OK" >> /var/log/ping.log
      echo 0 > "/tmp/${host}_fail"
    else
      echo "$(date +%F_%T) $host FAIL" >> /var/log/ping.log
      cnt=$(cat "/tmp/${host}_fail" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
      cnt=$((cnt+1))
      echo $cnt > "/tmp/${host}_fail"
      if ((cnt>=3)); then
        curl -s -X POST -d "{\"host\":\"$host\", \"status\":\"down\"}" http://example.com/webhook
      fi
    fi
  done < hosts.txt
  sleep 30
done

command:
backup_mysql(){
  local ts=$(date +%F_%H-%M-%S)
  local dump=/tmp/mysql_all_$ts.sql
  mysqldump --all-databases --single-transaction --quick --lock-tables=false > "$dump"
  gpg --yes --batch -r "$1" -o "$dump.gpg" -e "$dump"
  xz -9 "$dump.gpg"
  mv "$dump.gpg.xz" /backups/mysql_all_$ts.sql.gpg.xz
  rm -f "$dump"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/user_provision.log
while IFS=, read -r user email quota; do
  if id "$user" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "$(date) SKIP: $user exists" >> "$log"
    continue
  fi
  if useradd -m "$user"; then
    echo "$email" >> /etc/aliases && newaliases
    setquota -u "$user" 0 "$quota" 0 0 -a
    echo "$(date) SUCCESS: $user created with quota $quota" >> "$log"
  else
    echo "$(date) FAIL: could not create $user" >> "$log"
  fi
done < users.csv

#!/usr/bin/env bash
consec=0

  usage=$(mpstat 1 1 | awk '/Average/ {print 100-$NF}')
  ts=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
  echo "$ts CPU: ${usage}%" >> /tmp/cpu.log
  if (( $(echo "$usage > 90" | bc -l) )); then
    ((consec++))

  else
    consec=0
  fi
  sleep 5
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/syslog
max=$((100*1024*1024))
if (( $(stat -c%s "$log") > max )); then
  mv "$log" "$log.1"
  gzip "$log.1"
  touch "$log"
  chown syslog:adm "$log"
  chmod 640 "$log"
fi

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
max_jobs=4
while read -r url; do
  ((i=i%max_jobs)); ((i++==0)) && wait
  {
    attempts=0
    while ((attempts<3)); do
      if curl -O "$url"; then
        echo "$(date '+%F %T') SUCCESS $url" >> download.log
        break
      else
        ((attempts++))
        sleep 2
      fi
    done
    if ((attempts==3)); then
      echo "$(date '+%F %T') FAIL $url" >> download.log
    fi
  } &
 done < urls.txt
wait

inotifywait -m -e create --format '%w%f' /var/spool/queue | while read -r file; do

done

dockerize_repo(){
  local repo=$1
  local dir=$(mktemp -d)
  git clone "$repo" "$dir"
  pushd "$dir" >/dev/null
  local sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
  local name=$(basename "$repo" .git)

  popd >/dev/null

}

Write a script that, for each running Docker container, extracts its IP address (from docker inspect), pings it once, and records the latency (or timeout) to /tmp/container_latency.log with timestamps.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/tmp/container_latency.log
docker ps -q | while read cid; do
  name=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Name}}' "$cid" | sed 's|^/||')
  ip=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' "$cid")
  if ping -c1 -W1 "$ip" &>/dev/null; then
    rtt=$(ping -c1 -W1 "$ip" | grep 'time=' | awk -F'time=' '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1)
    echo "$(date +%F-%T) $name $ip $rtt ms" >> "$log"
  else
    echo "$(date +%F-%T) $name $ip timeout" >> "$log"
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
threshold=$((10*1024*1024)) # in KB
size=$(du -sk /var/lib/mysql | cut -f1)
if [ $size -gt $threshold ]; then
  mv /var/log/mysql/error.log /var/log/mysql/error.log.old
  systemctl restart mysql
  echo "MySQL logs rotated at $(date)" >> /var/log/mysql/rotate.log
fi

    echo "$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') SUCCESS $url" >> "$log"

  fi
done < urls.txt

Write a Bash script that monitors disk usage of /home, and when usage exceeds 80%, automatically moves the oldest files (by modification time) from /home/user/Downloads to /archive until usage drops below 70%, logging each move.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
THRESH_HIGH=80
THRESH_LOW=70
while :; do
  usage=$(df --output=pcent /home | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
  if (( usage > THRESH_HIGH )); then
    while (( usage > THRESH_LOW )); do
      oldest=$(find /home/user/Downloads -type f -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -n | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2-)
      [ -z "$oldest" ] && break
      mv "$oldest" /archive/ && echo "$(date +'%F %T') Moved $oldest to /archive" >> /var/log/disk_cleanup.log
      usage=$(df --output=pcent /home | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
    done
  fi
  sleep 300
done

Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, fetches each with curl (timeout 10s), saves the HTTP status code and content length to a tab‑separated file results.tsv, and retries failed downloads up to 2 times.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
while IFS= read -r url; do
  attempts=0
  while ((attempts<3)); do
    resp=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}\t%{size_download}\n" -o /dev/null --max-time 10 "$url")
    code=$(echo "$resp" | cut -f1)
    size=$(echo "$resp" | cut -f2)
    if [[ $code -ge 200 && $code -lt 400 ]]; then
      echo -e "$url\t$code\t$size" >> results.tsv
      break
    else
      ((attempts++))
    fi
  done
done < urls.txt

Write a Bash script that reads a list of package names from packages.txt, checks if each is installed (using dpkg or rpm depending on distro), installs missing ones via apt or yum, logs each action to /var/log/pkg_install.log, and sends a summary email at the end.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/pkg_install.log
summary=""
while read -r pkg; do
  if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dpkg -l "$pkg" &>/dev/null && installed=1 || installed=0
    installer='apt-get install -y'
  elif command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rpm -q "$pkg" &>/dev/null && installed=1 || installed=0
    installer='yum install -y'
  else
    echo "Unsupported distro" | tee -a "$log"
    exit 1
  fi
  if (( installed )); then
    echo "$(date) INFO: $pkg already installed" | tee -a "$log"
    summary+="$pkg: already installed\n"
  else
    if $installer "$pkg"; then
      echo "$(date) INFO: $pkg installed successfully" | tee -a "$log"
      summary+="$pkg: installed\n"
    else
      echo "$(date) ERROR: failed to install $pkg" | tee -a "$log"
      summary+="$pkg: failed\n"
    fi
  fi
done < packages.txt
echo -e "$summary" | mailx -s "Package installation summary" admin@example.com

hash_check(){
  dir="$1"
  ext="$2"
  find "$dir" -type f -name "*.$ext" | while read -r f; do
    sha256sum "$f" > "${f}.sha256"
  done
  echo "Verification results:"

  done

  semaphore=$(mktemp -u)
  mkfifo "$semaphore"
  exec 3<>"$semaphore"
  for ((i=0;i<5;i++)); do echo >&3; done
  for h in "${hosts[@]}"; do
    read -u3
    {
      if ping -c1 -W1 "$h" &>/dev/null; then
        ((reachable++))
      else
        ((unreachable++))
      fi
      echo >&3
    } &
  done
  wait
  exec 3>&-
  echo "Reachable: $reachable, Unreachable: $unreachable"
}

watch_fatal(){
  local logfile="$1"
  tail -F "$logfile" |\
    grep --line-buffered -C5 "FATAL" |\
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      echo "$line" >> /tmp/fatal_context.txt

  # Background monitor; send email when file grows

    while read -r _; do

        mail -s "Fatal detected" admin@example.com < /tmp/fatal_context.txt
        > /tmp/fatal_context.txt
      fi
    done
}

Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl (retry up to 3 times on failure), computes the MD5 hash of the downloaded file, and stores the mapping URL→hash in a JSON file results.json.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mapfile -t urls < urls.txt
declare -A results
for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  fname=$(basename "$url")
  attempts=0
  until curl -L -o "$fname" "$url"; do
    ((attempts++))
    ((attempts==3)) && echo "Failed $url" && break
    sleep $((attempts*2))
  done
  if [[ -f "$fname" ]]; then
    hash=$(md5sum "$fname" | awk '{print $1}')
    results["$url"]="$hash"
  fi
done
printf '{\n' > results.json
for k in "${!results[@]}"; do
  printf '  "%s": "%s"%s\n' "$k" "${results[$k]}" "," >> results.json
done
sed -i '$ s/,$//' results.json
printf '}\n' >> results.json

#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p /tmp/downloads
while read -r url; do
  fname=$(basename "$url")

    echo "$(date +%F_%T) SUCCESS $url" >> download.log

    echo "$(date +%F_%T) FAIL $url" >> download.log
  fi
done < urls.txt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/user_create.log
while IFS=, read -r user uid; do
  if id "$user" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "$(date): $user already exists" >> "$log"
    continue
  fi
  if useradd -u "$uid" -G sudo "$user"; then
    echo "$(date): Created $user with UID $uid" >> "$log"
  else
    echo "$(date): Failed to create $user" >> "$log"
  fi
done < users.csv

#!/usr/bin/env bash
while read -r url; do
  ((i=i%3)); ((i++==0)) && wait
  (
    for attempt in {1..3}; do
      curl -f -O "$url" && echo "SUCCESS: $url" >> download.log && break
      echo "Attempt $attempt failed for $url" >&2
      sleep 2
    done

  ) &
done < urls.txt

mkdir -p "$backup_dir"

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
while :; do
  rows=$(mysql -N -B -e "SELECT id, payload FROM jobs WHERE processed=0 LIMIT 10;")
  [[ -z $rows ]] && sleep 10 && continue
  while read -r id payload; do
    response=$(curl -s -X POST -d "$payload" https://api.example.com/handle)
    if [[ $response == *"success"* ]]; then
      mysql -e "UPDATE jobs SET processed=1 WHERE id=$id;"
      echo "$(date): Processed $id" >> job.log
    else
      echo "$(date): Failed $id - $response" >> job_error.log
    fi
  done <<< "$rows"
  sleep 1
done

Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl (max 5 concurrent downloads), saves them with their original filename, and retries failed downloads up to 2 times.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
xargs -a urls.txt -n1 -P5 -I{} bash -c '
  url="{}"
  fname=$(basename "$url")
  attempts=0
  while (( attempts < 3 )); do
    if curl -f -L -o "$fname" "$url"; then
      echo "Downloaded $fname"
      break
    else
      ((attempts++))
      echo "Retry $attempts for $url"
    fi
  done
'

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
docker events --filter 'event=pull' --format '{{json .}}' |
  while read -r event; do
    name=$(echo "$event" | jq -r .Actor.Attributes.name)
    size=$(docker image inspect "$name" --format '{{.Size}}')
    ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    echo "$ts,$name,$size" >> /var/log/docker_image_pulls.log
done

while read -r url; do
  grep -q "^$url " hashes.txt && continue

#!/usr/bin/env bash
logfile="/var/log/docker_containers.csv"
# Ensure header exists
[[ -f $logfile ]] || echo "container_id,image,start_time" > $logfile

while docker events --filter 'event=start' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Image}} {{.Time}}' --since 0s; do
  docker events --filter 'event=start' --format '{{.ID}},{{.Image}},{{.Time}}' | while IFS=, read -r id img ts; do
    echo "${id},${img},$(date -d @${ts} +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S)" >> $logfile
  done
  sleep 1
done &
# Logrotate config (place in /etc/logrotate.d/docker_containers)
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/logrotate.d/docker_containers
/var/log/docker_containers.csv {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
}

command:
rotate_logs(){
  dir="$1"
  max=$2
  find "$dir" -type f -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -exec gzip {} \;
  compressed=$(ls -1t "$dir"/*.log.gz 2>/dev/null)
  count=0
  for f in $compressed; do
    ((count++))
    if [ $count -gt $max ]; then
      rm -f "$f"
    fi
  done
}

Write a Bash function that accepts a PID, monitors its open file descriptors every second, writes a CSV of timestamp, FD count, and total bytes read/written to /tmp/fd_monitor.csv, and stops when the process exits.
command:
monitor_fds(){
  pid=$1
  echo "timestamp,fd_count,bytes_read,bytes_written" > /tmp/fd_monitor.csv
  while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do
    ts=$(date +%s)
    fd=$(ls /proc/$pid/fd | wc -l)
    io=$(cat /proc/$pid/io 2>/dev/null || echo -e "read_bytes: 0\nwrite_bytes: 0")
    read_bytes=$(echo "$io" | awk -F': ' '/read_bytes/ {print $2}')
    write_bytes=$(echo "$io" | awk -F': ' '/write_bytes/ {print $2}')
    echo "$ts,$fd,$read_bytes,$write_bytes" >> /tmp/fd_monitor.csv
    sleep 1
  done
}

command:
retry_cmd() {
  local cmd="$1"
  local retries=$2
  local delay=1
  for ((i=0;i<=retries;i++)); do
    eval "$cmd" && return 0
    ((i==retries)) && break
    sleep $delay
    delay=$((delay*2))
  done
  return 1

fi

while true; do
  usage=$(mpstat 1 1 | awk '/Average/ {print 100 - $NF}')

  if (( $(echo "$usage > 80" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "$ts CPU $usage%" >> /var/log/high_cpu.log

    if ((consec>=3)); then

CPU usage exceeded 80% for 3 consecutive checks.
Last reading: $ts ($usage%)

    fi
  else
    consec=0
  fi
  sleep 5
done

Write a Bash function that takes a process name pattern, finds the oldest matching process, and sends it a SIGTERM, then waits up to 10 seconds for it to exit before sending SIGKILL.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
terminate_oldest(){
  local pattern="$1"
  pid=$(ps -eo pid,etime,comm --no-headers |\
        awk -v pat="$pattern" '$3 ~ pat {print $1,$2}' |\
        sort -k2 | head -n1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
  [[ -z $pid ]] && return 1
  kill -TERM "$pid"
  for i in {1..10}; do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    sleep 1
done
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid"
}
# Usage: terminate_oldest "myservice"

prompt: Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl (max 5 retries, 10 s timeout), saves to /data with filenames based on SHA256 of the URL, and logs successes and failures.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/downloads.log
while read -r url; do
  fname=$(echo -n "$url" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  for i in {1..5}; do
    if curl -m 10 -sSL "$url" -o "/data/$fname"; then
      echo "$(date +%F_%T) SUCCESS $url -> $fname" >> $log; break
    else
      echo "$(date +%F_%T) RETRY $i $url" >> $log
    fi
  done
  if (( i == 5 )); then
    echo "$(date +%F_%T) FAILURE $url" >> $log
  fi
done < urls.txt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
in_dir="/opt/incoming"
proc_dir="/opt/processed"
log_file="/var/log/invalid_csv.log"
while true; do
  inotifywait -e close_write,moved_to "$in_dir" --format "%f" | while read file; do
    if [[ "$file" == *.csv ]]; then
      if awk -F',' 'NF!=5{exit 1}' "$in_dir/$file"; then
        mv "$in_dir/$file" "$proc_dir/"
      else
        echo "$(date +%F_%T) Invalid: $file" >> "$log_file"
      fi
    fi
  done
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
threshold=5368709120
while true; do
  free=$(df --output=avail /var | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  if (( free < threshold )); then
    report=$(du -h --max-depth=1 /var | sort -hr | head -5)
    echo -e "Subject: Low Disk Space on /var\n\nFree space: $(numfmt --to=iec $free)\nTop directories:\n$report" | sendmail admin@example.com
  fi
  sleep 300
done

Create a Bash function that accepts a directory and a regex, recursively finds files matching the regex, replaces all occurrences of the word "ERROR" with "WARN" using sed, and logs the changes to a timestamped file in /var/log/patches/
command:
patch_errors(){
  dir="$1"
  regex="$2"
  logdir="/var/log/patches"
  mkdir -p "$logdir"
  logfile="$logdir/patch_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log"
  find "$dir" -type f -regextype posix-extended -regex "$regex" -print0 |
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
      if grep -q "ERROR" "$f"; then
        sed -i 's/ERROR/WARN/g' "$f"
        echo "$(date +%F%T) patched $f" >> "$logfile"
      fi
    done
}

Write a Bash script that rotates logs: compresses logs older than 7 days with gzip, moves them to /var/log/archive, and creates a new empty log file with the same name, preserving permissions.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
logdir="/var/log"
archive_dir="/var/log/archive"
mkdir -p "$archive_dir"
find "$logdir" -type f -name "*.log" -mtime +7 | while read log; do
  perm=$(stat -c %a "$log")
  gzip -c "$log" > "$archive_dir/$(basename "$log").gz"
  chmod $perm "$archive_dir/$(basename "$log").gz"
  : > "$log"
  chmod $perm "$log"
  echo "Rotated $log" >> "$logdir/rotate.log"
 done

Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl showing a progress bar, retries up to 3 times on failure, and stores the HTTP status code of each request in a CSV file called download_status.csv.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf 'url,status\n' > download_status.csv
while IFS= read -r url; do
  attempts=0
  while ((attempts<3)); do
    ((attempts++))
    code=$(curl -w "%{http_code}" -L -s -S --progress-bar "$url" -o "$(basename "$url")" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ $code -ge 200 && $code -lt 400 ]]; then
      printf '%s,%s\n' "$url" "$code" >> download_status.csv
      break
    fi
  done
  if ((attempts==3)); then
    printf '%s,FAIL\n' "$url" >> download_status.csv
  fi
done < urls.txt

Create a Bash function called rotate_logs that rotates logs in /var/log/myapp/, keeping the last 7 compressed archives and deleting older ones. The function should be safe to run via cron.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
rotate_logs(){
    local dir="/var/log/myapp"
    local prefix="myapp.log"
    local timestamp=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
    if [[ -f "$dir/$prefix" ]]; then
        mv "$dir/$prefix" "$dir/${prefix}.$timestamp"
        gzip "$dir/${prefix}.$timestamp"
    fi
    # Keep only the 7 most recent .gz files
    ls -1t "$dir/${prefix}."*.gz | tail -n +8 | xargs -r rm -f
}
# Example usage: rotate_logs

Create a bash function "retry" that runs a given command up to 5 times with exponential backoff (1s,2s,4s,8s) until it succeeds, returning the command's exit status.
command:
retry(){
  local max=5; local i=0; local delay=1
  while (( i < max )); do
    "$@" && return 0
    ((i++))
    sleep $delay
    ((delay*=2))
  done
  return 1
}

Generate a command that lists all Docker containers that have been stopped for more than 24 hours, and removes them after confirming with the user.
command:
docker ps -a --filter "status=exited" --format "{{.ID}} {{.CreatedAt}}" | while read id date; do
  if [[ $(date -d "$date" +%s) -lt $(date -d "24 hours ago" +%s) ]]; then
    echo "Container $id stopped at $date"
    read -p "Delete this container? [y/N] " ans
    [[ $ans == [Yy]* ]] && docker rm "$id"
  fi
done
